items.title: Domestic petrol supply falls 20.6%, imports rise in July — NMDPRA
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Average daily petrol supply from domestic refineries fell by 20.6 per cent to 25.8 million litres in July 2026, from 32.5 million litres per day recorded in June, data from the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) has shown. The latest figures obtained from the Authority’s monthly oil and gas data also showed that the decline in domestic supply was partly offset by an increase in imported petrol, which rose to 19.7 million litres per day in July from 18.1 million litres per day in June. Combined domestic and imported petrol supply consequently stood at an average of 45.5 million litres per day in July, down 10.1 per cent from the 50.6 million litres supplied daily in June. The July figures marked the second consecutive monthly decline in total petrol supply, after combined supply rose from 47.4 million litres per day in May to 50.6 million litres in June. The NMDPRA data showed considerable fluctuations in domestic petrol supply during the first seven months of the year. Domestic supply stood at 40.1 million litres per day in January before falling sharply by 26.7 per cent to 29.4 million litres in February. Supply recovered to 34.2 million litres per day in March, representing a 16.3 per cent increase from February, and rose further to 40.7 million litres in April, up 19 per cent month-on-month. The upward trend continued in May when domestic petrol supply reached a seven-month high of 41.5 million litres per day, an increase of 2 per cent over April. However, supply declined by 21.7 per cent to 32.5 million litres per day in June before falling by another 20.6 per cent to 25.8 million litres in July. The July figure was the lowest domestic petrol supply recorded in the seven-month period and was 37.1 per cent below the January level. Meanwhile, imported petrol supply followed a different trajectory. The country received an average of 24.8 million litres of imported petrol daily in January, the highest monthly volume recorded during the period under review. Imports plunged by 87.9 per cent to just three million litres per day in February. They subsequently increased to 5.9 million litres in March, representing a 96.7 per cent month-on-month rise. Imports declined again to 3.7 million litres per day in April, before rising by 59.5 per cent to 5.9 million litres in May. A significant increase was recorded in June, when imported petrol supply more than tripled to 18.1 million litres per day, representing a 206.8 per cent increase over May. The upward trend continued in July, although at a much slower pace, with imports rising 8.8 per cent to 19.7 million litres per day. Despite the increase, July imports remained 20.6 per cent below the 24.8 million litres per day recorded in January. Monthly supply picture In January, total petrol supply averaged 64.9 million litres per day, comprising 40.1 million litres of domestic supply and 24.8 million litres of imports. February recorded the lowest combined supply in the seven-month period at 32.4 million litres per day, as domestic supply fell to 29.4 million litres while imports dropped to three million litres. Combined supply recovered to 40.1 million litres in March and 44.4 million litres in April before reaching 47.4 million litres in May. The June increase to 50.6 million litres per day was driven largely by the sharp rise in imports, which climbed to 18.1 million litres, even as domestic supply fell to 32.5 million litres. In July, total supply declined to 45.5 million litres per day. Domestic refineries accounted for 25.8 million litres, or about 56.7 per cent of total supply, while imports accounted for 19.7 million litres, or 43.3 per cent. The post Domestic petrol supply falls 20.6%, imports rise in July — NMDPRA appeared first on Vanguard News .

According to the Police, Michael Ayitey Okai is currently in custody and assisting with investigations into the matter. The Accra Regional Police Command said its investigations are focused on establishing the circumstances surrounding the alleged threat and determining the appropriate action in accordance with the law. In a statement issued by the Regional Public Affairs Unit, the Police urged the public to refrain from spreading unverified information concerning the case while investigations are ongoing. items.title: La croissance de l’OCDE atteint 0,5 % au deuxième trimestre 2026
items.description: La croissance économique dans la zone de l'Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques (OCDE) s’est inscrite en légère hausse pour s’établir à 0,5 % au 2ème trimestre 2026, contre 0,4 % au trimestre précédent, selon des estimations de l’Organisation, publiées lundi. Cette évolution reflète une situation contrastée parmi les 30 pays de l’OCDE pour lesquels des données étaient disponibles, indique l’organisation, notant que 27 pays ont enregistré une croissance au 2ème trimestre, à des rythmes toutefois variables, tandis que 3 pays n’ont enregistré aucune variation du PIB. Dans les pays du G7, la croissance du PIB a ralenti à 0,3 % au T2-2026, contre 0,4 % au trimestre précédent, sous l’effet d’un ralentissement de la croissance dans cinq pays du G7. Il s’agit de l’Allemagne, de 0,4 % à 0,2 % ; l’Italie, de 0,3 % à 0,2 % ; le Japon, de 0,5 % à 0,3 % ; le Royaume-Uni, de 0,6 % à 0,4 % ; et les États-Unis, de 0,5 % à 0,4 %. Au Japon, cette décélération s’explique principalement par la stagnation de la consommation privée, le déstockage et le recul de l’investissement, fait savoir l’OCDE, ajoutant qu’au Royaume-Uni, l’affaiblissement de la consommation privée et le recul de la consommation des administrations publiques ont impacté l’activité économique. Aux États-Unis, le ralentissement de la croissance s’explique principalement par une croissance plus faible des exportations, le déstockage et une baisse de la consommation des administrations publiques. À l’inverse, la croissance au Canada s’est accélérée, passant de zéro au T1 à 0,8 % au T2. En France, le PIB a renoué avec la croissance avec +0,2 % au T2, après une contraction de 0,1 % au T1. Parmi les autres pays de l’OCDE pour lesquels des données étaient disponibles, l’Irlande a enregistré la plus forte croissance du PIB en glissement trimestriel au T2, à 3,9 %. À l’autre extrémité du classement, le PIB est resté inchangé en Autriche, en Belgique et au Chili. En glissement annuel, la croissance du PIB dans la zone OCDE a atteint 2,3 % au T2 2026, contre 1,7 % au T1. Parmi les économies du G7, les États-Unis ont enregistré la plus forte croissance annuelle du PIB, à 2,1 %, tandis que le Japon a enregistré la plus faible, à 0,5 %. items.title: Niger : Niamey accueille la première session du parlement de la Confédération des États du Sahel
items.description: Niamey accueille, a compter de ce 24 août, la premiere session du parlement de la Confederation des etats du Sahel (AES) au centre des conferences Mahatma Gandhi de Niamey, a rapporte l'ANP. Cette derniere a precise que le parlement de l'AES etait constitue de 45 deputes, soit 15 representants par pays. evenement qui constitue une « etape majeure dans le processus d'operationnalisation et de consolidation de notre espace communautaire », a salue le Premier ministre nigerien, Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine, cite par APA News, present lors de la session inaugurale. Selon la meme source, le chef du gouvernement nigerien a rappele que la creation de l'AES traduisait la volonte du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger de « bâtir un espace souverain, solidaire et integre », notamment fonde sur la defense et la securite, la diplomatie ainsi que le developpement economique et social. Pour sa part, le Journal du Mali a souligne que cette rencontre a Niamey « n'installe pas, pour le moment, un Parlement supranational disposant du pouvoir de voter des lois directement applicables dans les trois pays ». « Leur mission consiste a deliberer et a emettre des avis sur les sujets soumis par le College des chefs d'etat ou concernant la vie de la Confederation », peut-on encore lire sur le site d'information francophone, qui evoque des travaux pouvant porter sur « la defense, la securite, la diplomatie, le developpement et les autres questions d'interet commun ».

items.title: Oppong Nkrumah heads back to Supreme Court over legal vacation ruling
items.description: Ofoase-Ayirebi Member of Parliament Kojo Oppong Nkrumah is seeking a review of the decision by Justice Gabriel Scott Pwamang dismissing his application to halt the conduct of criminal trials by selected High Court judges during the legal vacation. Mr Oppong Nkrumah is asking the Supreme Court to reverse the ruling delivered by Justice Pwamang, who sat as a Justice on Friday, August 21, 2026, and rejected the interlocutory injunction application. The development marks the latest stage in Mr Oppong Nkrumah’s legal challenge to the Chief Justice’s administrative warrants authorising selected High Court judges to conduct criminal proceedings during the annual legal vacation, which runs from August 1 to September 30. Challenge to vacation trials Mr Oppong Nkrumah invoked the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court earlier this month, challenging the decision by Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie to permit selected judges to sit during the vacation to hear criminal cases. His substantive case argues that the arrangement raises constitutional questions, including concerns over equality before the law and the proper exercise of administrative discretion. He subsequently applied for an interlocutory injunction to suspend the operation of the warrants until the Supreme Court had determined the substantive constitutional challenge. Justice Pwamang, however, dismissed the application, holding that Mr Oppong Nkrumah had not established a sufficiently strong case to warrant the interim relief. The Court also rejected the argument that the arrangement was discriminatory, noting that the warrants authorised the affected judges to conduct cases pending before their respective courts. “It is clear on the face of the warrant that the judges are supposed to conduct all cases pending in their courts,” the Court said. Justice Pwamang further held that the fact that criminal trials were not ordinarily conducted during the legal vacation did not mean the administration of justice could not be advanced during that period. Substantive case remains The dismissal of the injunction application does not bring Mr Oppong Nkrumah’s broader constitutional challenge to an end. The substantive case questioning the constitutionality of the Chief Justice’s warrants remains pending before the Supreme Court. Mr Oppong Nkrumah has maintained that his objection is not to the trial of accused persons but to the decision to conduct full criminal trials during the legal vacation under the current arrangement. His lawyer, Frank Davies, previously argued that the continuation of trials could affect accused persons’ rights to fair representation, particularly where lawyers may not be available during the vacation. The legal challenge has also generated a public debate over the purpose of the annual legal vacation and the extent to which the Judiciary can deploy administrative measures to accelerate the determination of criminal cases. The Chief Justice’s position, as reflected in the warrants and the arguments advanced on behalf of the respondents, is that the arrangement is intended to facilitate the speedy disposal of criminal matters. The latest application by Mr Oppong Nkrumah will now put the Supreme Court’s earlier decision under renewed scrutiny, while the substantive constitutional questions remain to be determined.

items.title: USFP : les investitures régionales provoquent des tensions internes
items.description: Les investitures de l’Union socialiste des forces populaires pour les prochaines législatives suscitent des remous au sein du parti. Derrière les désaccords sur les candidatures se profilent des interrogations sur les critères de sélection, la place des contributions financières et les règles encadrant la procédure. La direction assume ses choix, tandis que plusieurs militantes demandent des explications et davantage de transparence. La désignation des têtes de listes régionales de l’USFP pour les législatives du 23 septembre 2026 suscite des contestations au sein du parti. Démission, suspension d’adhésion et menace de recours judiciaires interviennent sur fond d’interrogations concernant les critères de sélection et la place accordée aux contributions financières. Le Bureau politique défend, de son côté, une procédure conforme aux règles internes du parti et rejette les accusations formulées par certaines militantes. La contestation prend de l’ampleur La situation s’est tendue après l’approbation, par le Bureau politique, des travaux des commissions chargées de statuer sur les candidatures aux circonscriptions régionales. Réuni samedi, l’organe dirigeant de l’USFP a validé à l’unanimité les décisions prises par les commissions, affirmant qu’elles avaient été arrêtées conformément aux statuts, au règlement intérieur et à la procédure spécifique mise en place pour ces investitures. Selon le communiqué du parti, cette procédure avait été publiée et portée à la connaissance des militantes et militants. L’USFP souligne également qu’aucun recours n’aurait été introduit depuis le dépôt des candidatures. Le Bureau politique salue ainsi le travail des différents organes impliqués et l’attitude qu’il qualifie de « fraternelle » des militantes n’ayant pas obtenu l’investiture. Cette présentation est toutefois contestée par plusieurs protagonistes de la procédure. Le Bureau politique a notamment annoncé avoir accepté la démission de Raja El Bekkali Taheri, sans détailler les motifs de son départ, se limitant à indiquer qu’il en tirait « les conséquences qui s’imposent ». Le cas de Meriem Jamal El Idrissi a, en revanche, fait l’objet d’une réponse beaucoup plus détaillée. Membre du conseil national et du secrétariat national des femmes socialistes, celle-ci a renoncé à son appartenance au parti après avoir contesté les résultats de la commission chargée de statuer sur les candidatures. Des accusations que la direction rejette Dans une lettre adressée à la direction du parti, Meriem Jamal El Idrissi avait demandé l’ouverture d’une enquête sur des soupçons de versements d’argent en contrepartie d’investitures sur les listes régionales. Elle relatait notamment avoir entendu, avant son passage devant la commission, des candidates évoquer des demandes portant sur les montants qu’elles seraient disposées à consacrer à la campagne électorale. Elle affirmait également que des montants compris entre 1,4 et 1,6 million de dirhams circulaient parmi les candidates. Elle précisait toutefois ne pas avoir vu elle-même les documents auxquels elle faisait référence et présentait ces éléments comme des informations devant être vérifiées, et non comme des faits établis. Le Bureau politique rejette catégoriquement cette lecture. Il accuse l’ancienne militante de diffuser des « allégations mensongères » portant atteinte à la crédibilité des institutions du parti, de s’en être prise aux membres de la commission et d’avoir formulé de graves accusations contre l’USFP. La direction affirme se réserver le droit de saisir la justice pour des faits susceptibles, selon elle, de constituer des infractions prévues par la loi. Elle défend parallèlement la régularité de la procédure et les critères arrêtés pour départager les candidates. La contribution financière au cœur des interrogations La contestation concerne également Manal Tekal, membre du Bureau politique, qui a mis en cause la manière dont les candidatures ont été départagées. Dans une lettre ouverte adressée au premier secrétaire de l’USFP, Idriss Lachgar, puis dans une publication diffusée sur sa page Facebook, Manal Tekal précise qu’elle ne conteste pas les quatre critères arrêtés par le Bureau politique. Elle remet plutôt en question leur application effective lors du processus de sélection et la manière dont ils auraient été pondérés par les commissions. La dirigeante affirme que ce qu’elle dit avoir constaté en tant que candidate, ainsi que les déclarations de candidates dans différentes régions et les témoignages de certains membres des commissions, l’amènent à considérer que la contribution financière n’aurait pas constitué un critère parmi quatre autres, mais aurait, selon elle, pris une place « unique et décisive » dans la sélection. Ces affirmations ne sont toutefois accompagnées, à ce stade, d’aucun document rendu public permettant d’établir l’existence d’un système de « l’argent contre l’investiture ». Manal Tekal demande précisément que la procédure soit soumise à vérification. Elle réclame notamment l’accès aux procès-verbaux des commissions chargées de statuer, aux grilles d’évaluation et de notation, si elles existent, ainsi qu’aux éléments objectifs ayant servi au classement des candidates. Elle souhaite que ces documents permettent de déterminer le poids effectivement accordé à chacun des critères annoncés, notamment la compétence, le parcours militant et le rayonnement politique et social. Une proposition de vérification indépendante Manal Tekal va plus loin en proposant la création d’une commission indépendante et neutre composée de compétences issues d’organismes ou d’institutions constitutionnelles spécialisées dans la gouvernance et l’intégrité. Cette instance serait chargée, selon sa proposition, d’examiner les dossiers des candidates, leurs présentations, leurs parcours professionnels et militants, ainsi que les procès-verbaux des commissions et les critères d’évaluation utilisés. L’objectif serait de vérifier de manière objective le respect des quatre critères adoptés par le Bureau politique et l’égalité de traitement entre les candidates. La membre du Bureau politique affirme ne réclamer ni avantage personnel ni réexamen du résultat en sa faveur. Elle dit demander que « la même règle soit appliquée à toutes » et que les décisions puissent être expliquées, justifiées et contrôlées. Le conflit porte aussi sur la suspension de Tekal Le Bureau politique a parallèlement décidé de suspendre temporairement l’adhésion de Manal Tekal jusqu’à la proclamation des résultats des élections. Une décision qu’elle conteste sur le fond comme sur la forme. Elle estime qu’un désaccord sur l’application d’une procédure interne ne saurait, à lui seul, justifier une sanction, notamment à l’encontre d’un membre d’un organe dirigeant. Elle demande que soient précisés le fondement réglementaire de la mesure, les griefs qui lui sont reprochés et les garanties de défense dont elle aurait dû bénéficier avant toute sanction. Manal Tekal soulève également une question plus large concernant le fonctionnement interne du parti. Elle affirme que le règlement organisationnel et le règlement intérieur n’auraient pas été mis à la disposition des militantes et militants depuis le dernier congrès, lequel aurait uniquement adopté les principes généraux devant encadrer ces textes. Elle appelle ainsi les membres du Bureau politique à réclamer eux-mêmes l’accès aux documents régissant la vie interne de l’USFP, estimant que la transparence des règles constitue une condition de la bonne gouvernance du parti. La possibilité d’un recours judiciaire Manal Tekal annonce enfin qu’elle entend conserver l’ensemble de ses droits organisationnels et juridiques. Elle envisage notamment de saisir les instances compétentes, voire la justice, afin de contester la suspension de son adhésion et d’examiner sa légalité, la compétence de l’organe ayant pris la décision ainsi que le respect des garanties de défense. De son côté, la direction de l’USFP maintient que les décisions des commissions ont été prises conformément à la procédure adoptée et validées à l’unanimité par le Bureau politique. Elle appelle désormais les militantes et militants à soutenir les candidats retenus et à se mobiliser en vue des élections législatives du 23 septembre. À moins d’un mois du scrutin, le différend reste donc concentré autour de la désignation des têtes de listes régionales, mais il met désormais en jeu à la fois les critères de sélection, la transparence de leur application et les règles disciplinaires internes au parti. Les accusations relatives au rôle des contributions financières demeurent, à ce stade, des affirmations portées par certaines militantes et contestées par la direction de l’USFP. Leur vérification passe désormais par les documents de la procédure, leur éventuelle mise à disposition et les recours que les intéressées décideront d’engager. The post USFP : les investitures régionales provoquent des tensions internes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Polémique en France, après la publication de clichés de militaires posant avec le drapeau de la Rhodésie
items.description: « Les armees francaises ne tolerent aucune manifestation a caractere raciste, supremaciste ou extremiste », a commente le ministere francais des Armees, cite ce 24 août par l'AFP, soulignant que les militaires « sont soumis a une exigence particuliere d'exemplarite et de neutralite », valable « egalement a leurs comportements et a leurs publications sur les reseaux sociaux ». Cette declaration survient au lendemain de la publication par Mediapart de deux photos de soldats, en uniforme, posant avec un drapeau « associe au supremacisme blanc ». Des photos qui auraient notamment ete postees sur le meme compte Instagram. Le media precise que ces militaires de l'armee francaise seraient sous le coup d'une procedure disciplinaire. Sur des photos partagées sur les réseaux sociaux, deux groupes de militaires français se sont affichés autour d’un drapeau de la Rhodésie, symbole associé aux suprémacistes blancs. Une procédure disciplinaire est en cours. https://t.co/rUAGmbOahP — Edwy Plenel (@edwyplenel) August 23, 2026 Quant au symbole en question, il s'agit du drapeau de la Rhodesie, un territoire secessionniste d'Afrique australe dirige de 1965 a 1979 par un gouvernement principalement blanc. Jamais reconnue par la communaute internationale, la Rhodesie a cesse d'exister avec l'independance du Zimbabwe. Toujours selon Mediapart , l'un des deux groupes serait issu du 2e regiment etranger d'infanterie de Nîmes, tandis que l'autre reunit des soldats en entraînement aux emirats arabes unis. « Les premiers elements de l'enquete permettent de confirmer que les deux evenements sont parfaitement disjoints, sans aucun lien ni entre les protagonistes, ni entre les activites », a commente le ministere.

items.title: Burkina : la 14e Semaine de la médecine traditionnelle prévue à Manga du 31 août au 5 septembre
items.description: Burkina : la 14e Semaine de la médecine traditionnelle prévue à Manga du 31 août au 5 septembre Ouagadougou, 24 août 2026 (AIB)- La 14e Semaine nationale de la médecine traditionnelle et alternative (SNMTA) se tiendra du 31 août au 5 septembre 2026 à Manga, dans la région du Nazinon, avec pour ambition de renforcer l’encadrement du secteur et de promouvoir une intégration responsable des pratiques traditionnelles dans le système de santé, a annoncé lundi le ministère de la Santé. Couplée à la 24e Journée africaine de la médecine traditionnelle (JAMT), prévue le 5 septembre, la 14e Semaine nationale de la médecine traditionnelle et alternative sera célébrée sur le thème : « Introduction des médicaments traditionnels améliorés dans les directives nationales de prise en charge des maladies au Burkina Faso : défis et opportunités pour l’atteinte de la souveraineté sanitaire ». L’information a été donnée lundi 24 août 2026 à Ouagadougou au cours d’une conférence presse. Le programme prévoit notamment une exposition de produits de médecine traditionnelle et alternative, des consultations et soins, des conférences, des ateliers et des sessions de renforcement des capacités. Une formation destinée aux infirmiers chefs de poste et aux pharmaciens de la région du Nazinon portera sur la conduite de l’enquête relative à l’évidence ethnomédicale. Sont également prévus une plantation d’arbres, un cross populaire suivi d’une séance d’aérobic, une nuit de la médecine traditionnelle et alternative, un don de sang et une clinique mobile de dépistage des cancers de la femme. Selon le chef de service de la médecine traditionnelle et des soins intégrés, Dr Kindo Esaïe, l’introduction des médicaments traditionnels améliorés dans les directives nationales doit être fondée sur des données scientifiques, une évaluation rigoureuse, une autorisation réglementaire, des normes de qualité et une pharmacovigilance effective. « La valorisation ne signifie pas l’absence de contrôle », a-t-il souligné, appelant à lutter contre les pratiques dangereuses, les allégations thérapeutiques non fondées et la publicité irrégulière. Le ministère entend renforcer la collaboration entre praticiens de la médecine traditionnelle et professionnels de la médecine conventionnelle, notamment à travers des mécanismes de référence et de recours. Il a invité les chercheurs à intensifier les travaux interdisciplinaires afin de produire des données fiables et de transformer les résultats de recherche en innovations adaptées aux besoins sanitaires du pays. Le chef de service de la médecine traditionnelle et des soins intégrés a appelé les populations à recourir à des tradi-praticiens reconnus et à rejoindre une structure de santé en cas d’urgence ou lorsque la situation dépasse les compétences du praticien traditionnel. Le ministère a enfin exhorté les médias à assurer une information responsable sur la médecine traditionnelle et à contribuer à la lutte contre les fausses promesses thérapeutiques. Pour Dr Kindo, le ministère travaille pour intégrer le service de médecine traditionnelle dans les hôpitaux. « Il y aura des services de médecine traditionnelle dans les hôpitaux et le malade aura le choix. Nous avons un comité dédié à cette intégration qui existe déjà. C’est une réalité qui va venir dans un avenir très proche », a-t-il ajouté. « Il y a 11 000 tradi-praticiens qui collaborent avec les centres de santé pour la prise en charge des maladies », a précisé le consultant en médecine traditionnelle Rémi Somé. Il a ajouté que les malades ont surtout recours à eux en cette période de paludisme et de morsures de serpents et qu’ils sont sollicités en première intention. Les responsables ont souligné la prolifération d’une certaine catégorie de praticiens se réclamant de la médecine traditionnelle et indiqué que le ministère de la Santé travaille au contrôle de la profession. « Préserver et valoriser nos savoirs, mais toujours dans la rigueur scientifique, la légalité, l’éthique et la protection de la santé publique », ont-ils poursuivi. Dr Kindo lance un appel aux chercheurs et aux institutions scientifiques à intensifier les travaux interdisciplinaires, à produire des données robustes et à accompagner la transformation responsable des résultats de recherche en innovations utiles, accessibles et adaptées aux priorités sanitaires nationales. Il rappelle aux populations que le recours à la médecine traditionnelle doit s’effectuer auprès de praticiens reconnus, dans le respect des indications et des règles de sécurité. Agence d’information du Burkina GIP/OB/yos

items.title: Benue ranching: NKST alleges 5,987 members killed, 753 churches destroyed
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Universal Reformed Christian Church, popularly known as NKST Church, has rejected the Federal Government’s proposed pilot ranching programme in Benue State, citing the killing of 5,987 of its members and the destruction of 753 worship centres during attacks blamed on armed herdsmen. The Church said the proposed ranching scheme was unacceptable in a state where thousands of indigenous people had been displaced by violence and many communities were still unable to return to their ancestral homes. The position was contained in a statement by the General Secretary of the NKST Synod Executive Committee, Rev. Ta Targba, who said the Church was not opposed to peaceful livestock farming but strongly rejected the use of Benue as a pilot state for the Federal Government’s ranching policy. Targba acknowledged the Federal Government’s efforts to find a lasting solution to the recurring herders-farmers crisis but argued that the priority should be the protection, restoration and resettlement of communities displaced by the violence. “Benue is not merely a geographical space available for government experimentation. The State is predominantly an agrarian society. Its land is the ancestral inheritance, economic foundation and livelihood of millions of people,” he said. According to him, generations of Benue people had cultivated their ancestral lands and established homes, churches, schools, hospitals, markets and other institutions on them. He said any policy involving land allocation, acquisition or conversion must take into consideration the ancestral rights, livelihoods, property rights and constitutional interests of the people occupying and cultivating the land. The NKST General Secretary questioned why Benue, which had suffered extensive displacement and destruction from violent conflicts, should be selected as a “laboratory” for a policy involving land allocation for the livestock economy allegedly associated with the crisis. “The NKST Church therefore asks: Why should a state whose people have suffered displacement and destruction because of violent conflict now be selected as a laboratory for a policy involving land allocation for the same livestock economy that has been at the centre of these conflicts? “The answer cannot be merely administrative. The people of Benue deserve to be heard,” he said. Targba stressed that the Church was speaking from experience, noting that its members and institutions had been directly affected by the prolonged violence in Benue and neighbouring states. “Over 5,987 of our members have been killed; 753 of our worship centres were destroyed by these marauders,” he stated. The Church called on the Federal Government to make the restoration and resettlement of displaced communities the foundation of any agricultural intervention in the state. It demanded adequate security to guarantee the safe and voluntary return of displaced persons, alongside the reconstruction of homes, schools, healthcare centres, markets, roads, water systems and churches destroyed during the violence. The NKST also urged the Federal Government to conduct a comprehensive inventory of destroyed public and faith-based institutions in affected communities, stressing that no ranch should be established on land from which people had been violently displaced. While reiterating its commitment to peace, reconciliation, justice and peaceful coexistence, the Church urged the Federal Government to reconsider the ranching plan and focus on its primary responsibility of protecting lives and property. Targba said the NKST remained willing to work with the Federal and state governments, traditional institutions, other churches, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to promote lasting peace, stressing that “restoration” must be at the centre of any government intervention in Benue. The post Benue ranching: NKST alleges 5,987 members killed, 753 churches destroyed appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Thousands gather at OVO Arena Wembley for MOGmusic’s ‘Back to Basics’ worship
items.description: Thousands of worshippers gathered at OVO Arena Wembley in London on Saturday, 22nd August, for MOGmusic’s Back to Basics Worship Experience. The gathering brought together worshippers from across the United Kingdom and beyond for an evening centred on worship, prayer and a call to spiritual revival. From the opening moments, the atmosphere built steadily as thousands lifted their voices together, setting the stage for an extended night of worship, prayer and reflection rooted in the vision behind Back to Basics: stripping away distractions and returning to the foundations of the Christian faith: Jesus, prayer, worship and surrender. The night featured a line-up of ministers and worship leaders, including Emmanuel Smith, Warehouse Worship, Israel Houghton, Ntokozo Mbambo and Joe Mettle, who each led the audience through distinct moments of praise and worship. Beyond the music, Back to Basics also created space for compassion in action. During the event, attendees were invited to support the work of Compassion, with a call for charitable donations and an opportunity for worshippers to translate their faith into practical generosity towards those in need. The initiative served as a reminder that worship extends beyond what happens within the walls of an arena and into how believers respond to the needs of others. When MOGmusic took to the stage, he thanked the thousands who had gathered at Wembley and briefly acknowledged his pastor, Apostle General Sam Korankye Ankrah, for his guidance and leadership. He then led the arena into the heart of the Back to Basics experience. Through songs and prayer, MOGmusic led those gathered at OVO Arena Wembley through an intense time of worship and intercession, with the evening taking on the atmosphere of a revival gathering. He brought to life the vision behind Back to Basics: stripping away distractions and returning to the foundations of the Christian faith: Jesus, prayer, worship and surrender. For MOGmusic, taking Back to Basics to Wembley represented a significant milestone in a ministry that began in Ghana and has continued to reach audiences around the world.

items.title: Agrobusiness, sécurité alimentaire… : à Niamone, la terre veut retenir ses enfants
items.description: À Tobor, la terre produit, forme et prépare une nouvelle génération d’entrepreneurs agricoles. Dans cette commune du département de Bignona, tous misent sur les terres disponibles, l’eau d’Affiniam et la formation agroécologique pour faire de l’agriculture un rempart contre l’exode vers l’Europe. ZIGUINCHOR – À peine franchi le portail du centre agroécologique de Tobor, le regard est happé par une scène inhabituelle. Ici, la terre semble devenir un lieu d’apprentissage, d’expérimentation et d’espoir. Des parcelles verdoyantes s’étendent dans l’enceinte du centre. Des plants sont bien entretenus. Plus loin, des jeunes habillés en t-shirts verts s’affairent autour de nouvelles pousses qu’ils mettent en terre avec application. À quelques mètres, d’autres découvrent les métiers liés aux énergies renouvelables, dont le solaire, tandis que l’aquaculture ouvre de nouvelles perspectives. Le centre agroécologique est ainsi devenu un point de convergence pour une jeunesse venue de Niamone, mais aussi de plusieurs régions du pays. Certains apprenants ont même fait le déplacement depuis Goudiry. A lire aussi : Pôle territoire Sud : une terre riche, mais sous-exploitée, selon une étude Tous partagent une même ambition : apprendre, produire et, surtout, pouvoir vivre de leur savoir-faire. Dans ce décor, les mains plongent dans la terre pendant que les esprits se forment. Pour Atab Badji, maire de Niamone, sa commune possède une réserve foncière nécessaire pour franchir ce cap. « Niamone dispose d’un potentiel foncier important, contrairement à Bignona et Ziguinchor. Nous sommes également situés à une position stratégique, à proximité des marchés gambien et bissau-guinéen. Et nous avons également la chance de disposer d’un centre de formation agroécologique », se glorifie l’élu territorial lors de la visite du ministre de l’Agriculture, Dr Cheikhou Oumar Bâ. Mais l’argument le plus fort, selon lui, se trouve dans les salles et les parcelles du centre. Les jeunes qui y sont formés. « Nous avons ici des jeunes qui peuvent devenir de véritables fermiers. Ils n’ont aucune raison d’aller chercher leur avenir en Europe. Ils disposent d’un centre agroécologique moderne, avec de bonnes conditions de formation et d’hébergement. Il nous appartient maintenant de les accompagner et de leur donner les moyens de réussir », insiste Atab Badji. Affiniam, le réservoir qui peut changer la donne À Niamone, la question foncière ne constitue pas le seul motif d’espoir. L’eau pourrait également jouer un rôle déterminant dans la transformation agricole de la commune. Pour cela, le maire pointe le potentiel du barrage d’Affiniam, récemment réhabilité. Une ressource qu’il considère comme un levier encore sous-exploité. « Notre commune compte onze villages et dispose de nombreuses potentialités. Nous ne sommes pas confrontés à un problème majeur d’accès à l’eau, grâce au barrage d’Affiniam. Il y reste encore environ 25 millions de mètres cubes d’eau non exploités qui pourraient contribuer fortement à notre objectif d’autosuffisance alimentaire », se réjouit Atab Badji. Pour l’édile, le plus difficile a déjà été réalisé avec la réhabilitation de l’ouvrage. Il faut désormais franchir l’étape suivante : amener l’eau jusqu’aux terres agricoles. « Le barrage a été réhabilité à coups de milliards. Il faut maintenant réaliser les investissements nécessaires pour connecter les champs au réseau d’eau. Une telle démarche permettrait de sécuriser la production et de donner aux agriculteurs les moyens de travailler dans de meilleures conditions », estime Atab Badji. Des terres disponibles, une réserve d’eau importante, une situation géographique avantageuse et une jeunesse en formation etc. L’équation est donc résolue. Il ne manque, selon le maire, qu’un ingrédient essentiel : l’investissement. « Les investisseurs qui cherchent une destination agricole doivent regarder du côté de Niamone. Investir ici, c’est exploiter un potentiel économique considérable, mais c’est aussi offrir une alternative à l’exode des jeunes vers l’Europe et vers d’autres destinations », plaide-t-il. Cette volonté de faire de la jeunesse un acteur du développement local ne date toutefois pas d’hier. Dès son arrivée à la tête de la commune, Atab Badji a lancé le projet « Un village, une vallée, une ASC, un champ ». L’ambition est de faire des associations sportives et culturelles (Asc) un véritable outil de mobilisation agricole. Dans les parcelles du centre agroécologique, les jeunes continuent de planter. Geste après geste, ils mettent en terre bien plus que de simples plants. Ils y matérialisent leur ambition de construire leur avenir ici, plutôt que de le chercher ailleurs. À Niamone, la bataille contre l’exode des jeunes pourrait ainsi commencer par une chose aussi simple qu’un geste de la main : planter, cultiver et récolter sur sa propre terre. Par Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: 23 lives lost to abandoned illegal mining pits in Ashanti Region – Regional Minister
items.description: At least 23 lives have been lost to abandoned illegal mining pits in the Ashanti Region, with a significant number of them being minors. Although 19 bodies have been retrieved from the open pits, the remaining four are still trapped deep in the pits. This was revealed by the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr Frank Amoakohene, during the commissioning of the new ultramodern office complex for the Minerals Commission in Kumasi. Speaking at the event, the Regional Minister recounted that 11 of the deceased are children. He noted that many of the victims were innocent residents who were attempting to access their farms but met their untimely deaths. “Twenty-three lives have been lost only because they were on their way to their farms and fell into pits that were left uncovered by miners within the various areas. Only 19 have been recovered from the pits; the remaining four we have not been able to recover,” he said. He added: “Eleven of them are children whose future has been cut short because someone, in his quest for money, left a pit uncovered within some of these areas that lead to farmlands.” As a result, Dr Amoakohene emphasised that the Regional Security Council, with support from the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, has begun reclamation efforts to cover all abandoned illegal mining pits dotted across several communities. “We have started reclamation efforts to cover these abandoned pits. The work is truly ongoing and we want to thank the Minister for that,” Dr Amoakohene noted as he called on stakeholders to support the initiative. He further noted that, through the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, the security services together with the Forestry Commission have been able to remove all permanent structures developed in the region’s forest reserves. Dr Amoakohene asserted that structures, including filling stations sited deep in forest reserves, have all been rendered non-operational to halt fuel supplies to illegal miners. “In times past, there used to be filling stations well established within forest reserves to support mining activities. As we speak now, there is no forest reserve in the Ashanti Region that has a filling station or any permanent structure,” he said. Dr Amoakohene also indicated that the government, in collaboration with the UK government, has erected permanent camps and structures along rivers in the region to be occupied by forest guards to safeguard the forests and water bodies.

items.title: Five wounded as transport unions’ members clash in Kwara
items.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin No fewer than five persons were reportedly injured during a clash between members of rival transport unions in Ilorin, Kwara State on Monday. Vanguard reliably gathered that pandemonium erupted around Idi-Araba and Itakudimo areas of the metropolis following an alleged attack on an office of the National Association of Road Transport Owners (NARTO). The incident forced residents and motorists to flee the area as the clash escalated. A resident of the area, Mr Mubaraq Bello, said they were at home when they suddenly saw some youths alight from tricycles armed with cutlasses and other dangerous weapons. According to him, the youths moved towards the NARTO office, with some allegedly throwing stones at the building. A NARTO member, Abubakar Olatunbosun, alleged that members of the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW), Road Transport Employers’ Association of Nigeria (RTEAN) and Tricycle Owners’ Association of Nigeria (TOAN) attacked them while they were on their way to the Police headquarters in Ilorin. Olatunbosun appealed to the Kwara State government to intervene in the matter, saying NARTO members respect the law and would not take the law into their own hands because Kwara is known for peace. He also alleged that over 100 tricycles belonging to their members had been seized by the other unions. A victim, Abdulwasiu Jamiu, alleged that members of the unions attacked them, forcefully took away their tricycles and inflicted injuries on some of them. Another victim, Lukman Iyanda, who reportedly sustained a broken hand, said he was attacked at Itakudimo while operating his tricycle. However, a member of RTEAN, who spoke on condition of anonymity, alleged that NARTO is an unregistered association and is not recognised by the government. Efforts to reach representatives of the other unions for their reactions were futile as of the time of filing this report. items.title: US removes Syria from state sponsor of terrorism list
items.description: The United States on Monday delisted Syria as a state sponsor of terrorism, rescinding a decades-old designation that had severely impeded investment. The US Department of State also revoked its designation of al-Nusrah Front — also known as Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) — as a global terrorist organization. The Treasury Department followed through with sanctions relief. “Today’s action will help foster additional investment in Syria to promote political and economic stability,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. Treasury said the moves were “in line with President (Donald) Trump’s promise to deliver sanctions relief to Syria.” But the agency stressed that its removal of restrictions on Syria “does not change Treasury’s posture with regards to countering global terrorism and our commitment to hold bad actors in Syria accountable.” HTS was earlier known as Al-Nusra Front and was formerly the branch of Al-Qaeda in Syria. But it broke ties with the jihadist group in 2016 and sought to soften its image. The United States had initially announced in July its intent to delist Syria as a state sponsor of terrorism, a move seen as a vote of confidence in leader Ahmed al-Sharaa. The step came as Trump met on the sidelines of a NATO summit in Turkey with Sharaa, a former jihadist who has sought to recast himself as a unifying figure after the 2024 toppling of the Assad family, which ruled with an iron fist for a half-century. AFP The post US removes Syria from state sponsor of terrorism list appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Catholic priest suspended after abandoning parish, Diocese says
items.description: The Catholic Diocese of Konongo-Mampong in the Ashanti region has suspended a priest indefinitely for allegedly abandoning his post without permission and becoming unreachable. The sanction bars him from performing priestly duties. The priest, Rev. Fr. Samuel Adapore, until now the Rector of St. Anthony of Padua Rectorate at Nkwantakese in the Ashanti Region, was handed a suspension with effect from Monday, 24 August 2026. The sanction was announced in a letter signed by the Bishop of the Diocese, Most Rev. John Opoku-Agyemang, and addressed to all clergy and the faithful. A suspension a divinis is a canonical penalty in the Catholic Church which forbids a cleric from administering sacraments publicly, including celebrating or concelebrating Mass or officiating at other liturgical services. What the Diocese alleges According to the letter published on Facebook, the decision was taken “with a heavy heart but a great sense of duty to Holy Mother Church” in consultation with the College of Consultors. The Diocese says Fr. Adapore took a unilateral decision to go on leave of absence and abandoned his pastoral ministry at Nkwantakese without legitimate permission. It also indicated that he removed all his personal belongings from the mission house at Nkwantakese without informing anyone. The statement added that as of now, the priest has “blocked all access to him” and that his immediate family members have maintained that none of them knows his whereabouts. The Bishop called on the faithful to remember the priest in their prayers. The Catholic Diocese of Konongo-Mampong, with its see in Mampong-Ashanti, covers a large part of the Ashanti region.

items.title: Financement durable de la santé en Afrique : le Sénégal réaffirme son engagement en faveur de la CSU
items.description: Le Sénégal a réaffirmé son engagement en faveur de la couverture sanitaire universelle (CSU) lors de la 76ᵉ session du Comité régional de l'Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) pour l'Afrique, qui se tient à Addis-Abeba du 24 au 28 août 2026. En marge de la 76ᵉ session du Comité régional de l'Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) pour l'Afrique, qui se tient à Addis-Abeba du 24 au 28 août 2026, le ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique a pris part au dialogue ministériel de haut niveau consacré au renforcement des systèmes de réglementation et de fabrication au niveau régional, au financement pérenne du secteur de la santé et au partenariat avec les organismes de santé multilatéraux et le secteur privé. « Réunissant le directeur régional de l’OMS, des ministres en charge des finances et ceux en charge de la Santé, ainsi que des représentants du secteur privé et des partenaires au développement, la session II relative au financement durable de la santé visait à définir des solutions pérennes pour la Région africaine », indique une note de la tutelle. Intervenant au cours de cette session, le Docteur Ibrahima SY a souligné l’importance de cette thématique, dans un contexte continental marqué par la pression budgétaire post-pandémie, le fardeau de la dette, la baisse de l’aide publique au développement et la multiplication des chocs sanitaires et climatiques. Selon la même source, le ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique a appelé à une responsabilité collective et individuelle pour garantir un accès universel à des services de santé de qualité. Il a, à cette occasion, partagé les réformes majeures engagées par le Sénégal pour accélérer les progrès vers la couverture sanitaire universelle (CSU). A lire aussi : Modernisation de l’offre de soins à Thiès : Plus de 690 millions de FCFA investis dans l’acquisition d’équipements médicaux Portée par la Stratégie nationale de transformation du système de santé (SNTSS) 2025-2034, la vision sénégalaise repose, rappelle la tutelle, sur une meilleure gestion des ressources et un modèle de financement plus résilient, inclusif et souverain. Ces orientations s’appuient sur des mécanismes de financement innovants, des réajustements budgétaires et un partenariat accru avec le secteur privé. En conclusion, le Docteur Ibrahima SY a réitéré l’engagement du gouvernement du Sénégal à augmenter les investissements publics dans la santé afin d'alléger le fardeau des dépenses de santé supporté par les ménages (les paiements directs) et de maximiser l’efficience des dépenses, conditions essentielles à la pérennité du système de santé. M. DIEME

items.title: Bagbin to admit Minority’s GoldBod motion but says debate must wait until after recall
items.description: Speaker of Parliament Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin says he intends to admit the Minority’s motion seeking scrutiny of the reported losses under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP). He has, however, made it clear that the matter cannot be debated during the ongoing emergency sitting. The Speaker said the motion, which was received at his office on August 21, had been personally reviewed and would be admitted to allow Parliament to thoroughly examine the claims surrounding the reported losses. “A few words on one thing mentioned by the minority leader, which has to do with the motion they have filed, which was received in my office on the 21st of August, 2026, just three days ago that it got to my office. I have gone through the motion myself and I intend to admit the motion because we have to at least have an end to litigation,” he said. Mr Bagbin said Parliament would have the opportunity to determine whether the reported figure constituted a loss or a cost after considering the matter. “As to whether it’s a loss or it’s a cost, this house will have the opportunity to go through it and please, Ghanaians are very intelligent people,” he said. The Speaker added that Ghanaians would be able to assess the arguments from both sides and reach their own conclusions. “They will listen, they will read in between the lines and they will make their decisions,” he said. His comments followed an intervention by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, who raised concerns over the reported GH¢22 billion equivalent of US$1.7 billion associated with the DGPP and linked the issue to the wider consequences of illegal mining. While indicating his intention to admit the Minority’s motion, Speaker Bagbin stressed that it could not form part of the business of the current emergency sitting. He reminded MPs that the House had been recalled specifically to consider three items of business outlined by President John Dramani Mahama. “These three items and then go back to the basic and fundamental function of representation and that is what recess is about,” he said. The Speaker said the motion could not be considered during the current one-week sitting because Parliament was no longer on recess when the motion was filed. “This is not a matter that can be considered within this one week because we are now sitting and the notice has come, we are not on recess,” he said. He consequently directed the Table Office to focus exclusively on the business for which Parliament had been recalled. “So please, as I stated, let’s make sure that we finish the business that was itemized by his excellency the President within the one week,” he said. “That is what we are here to do. We will not do any new business and so I am directing the table office to as much as possible focus on only this business. We are not going to have question time. We are not going to have any statements.” Speaker Bagbin also defended the principle of transparency in handling the GoldBod controversy, saying Parliament should not be seen as preventing the country from examining the matter. “But it’s not proper for us to try to cover up anything,” he said. He noted that Ghana’s Parliament was now part of the Open Governance Partnership and had taken steps to make its proceedings more open. “We are now part of the Open Governance Partnership and we have opened our parliament beyond any other parliament in Africa,” he said. According to him, both sides of the political divide had shown a willingness to engage and explain their positions on the matter. “So this is one of the things that from listening to both sides, not only in the house, even outside the house, both sides are willing to engage and to explain themselves and I don’t think that the speaker will be the one that will stand in the way of the country,” he said. The Speaker further explained that Parliament’s Standing Orders provide a mechanism for MPs to request a recall when the House is on recess. He cited Order 59, Rules 2 and 3, which he said allow members to request a recall, subject to consultation with the leadership of the House. He indicated that such a recall could potentially be organised within three or four days, but stressed that the procedure could not be invoked for the GoldBod motion during the current sitting because Parliament was already in session. For now, Parliament will proceed with the three items that prompted President Mahama’s request for the emergency sitting, while the Minority’s GoldBod motion awaits consideration at a later stage.

items.title: We’re seeking investigation, not conviction of Afenyo-Markin – Appiah Danquah defends ‘extortion’ petition
items.description: Director of Legal and Constitutional Affairs of the United Party, Andrew Appiah Danquah, has defended the party’s decision to petition multiple state institutions over the alleged extortion involving Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, insisting that the request is for an investigation and not a declaration of guilt. He said the seriousness of the allegations requires competent state institutions to establish the facts and determine whether the claims made by GoldBod CEO Sammy Gyamfi and NEIP CEO Eric Adjei are true. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Monday, August 24, Mr Appiah Danquah said the party’s petition is grounded in the need to protect Ghana’s constitutional democracy and ensure that public power is not allegedly used for private interests. “We are not participating because we have [concluded guilt]. We are participating because these serious allegations have been made against the Minority Leader, especially when the allegation brings up two very critical issues,” he said. According to him, the first issue is whether parliamentary authority may have been used for purposes other than those intended by the Constitution. He argued that Ghana’s constitutional framework requires public power to be exercised in the interest of the people and in accordance with the Constitution. The second concern, he said, relates to the criminal dimension of the allegations, particularly claims of extortion and the alleged use of public office for private financial gain. Mr Appiah Danquah acknowledged that the United Party’s petition names several institutions, including the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP), the Police, CHRAJ, the Attorney-General and the Speaker of Parliament. He, however, rejected suggestions that the petition was necessarily seeking multiple competing investigations into exactly the same matter. He explained that the institutions have different constitutional and statutory mandates and could examine different aspects of the allegations. “I’m not seeking institutions beyond institutions that are mandated under our Constitution to act,” he said. He pointed to CHRAJ’s mandate to investigate matters involving abuse of power, while arguing that allegations with a criminal character could fall within the remit of the police or the OSP, depending on the specific facts established. Mr Appiah Danquah further cited Section 79 of the Office of the Special Prosecutor Act, arguing that the OSP has jurisdiction over corruption-related offences involving public officers and that extortion may fall within the category of offences it can investigate. The United Party’s petition follows allegations publicly attributed to Sammy Gyamfi and subsequent claims by Eric Adjei involving Mr Afenyo-Markin. The petition asks the relevant institutions to establish whether the allegations are true and, if so, whether they disclose attempted extortion, corruption, abuse of public office or related offences. Mr Appiah Danquah stressed that the petition should not be interpreted as a finding of guilt against the Minority Leader. He said the investigation should instead establish the veracity of the allegations while ensuring that Afenyo-Markin is afforded the presumption of innocence and an opportunity to respond. “If the allegations are true, they may disclose an attempt to use political standing, parliamentary influence, access to information or the threat of reputational injury as instruments for extracting a substantial private financial benefit,” the petition states. The United Party has also called for the relevant agencies to obtain statements from Sammy Gyamfi and Eric Adjei, identify any alleged intermediaries and preserve relevant electronic, documentary, audiovisual and financial evidence. It wants the institutions to determine whether any public office, parliamentary position or institutional authority was allegedly used as leverage in connection with the purported demand. Mr Appiah Danquah maintained that the ultimate objective is to establish the facts. He said the investigation would serve both sides: substantiating the allegations if they are true, or clearing Afenyo-Markin if they cannot be proven.

items.title: Un Algérien rencontre Émilie à Saint-Omer, son OQTF l’empêche de l’épouser
items.description: Un nouveau mariage entre un ressortissant algérien et une citoyenne française a été refusé en France . Les deux tourtereaux se retrouvent face à un dispositif administratif et judiciaire compliqué qui les empêche d’officialiser leur union. Selon La Voix Du Nord, il s’agit de Mouloud Kaddour Djebbar, 40 ans, qui est originaire de Boukadir, dans la wilaya de Chlef, dans l’Ouest algérien, et d'Émilie Raoult, 36 ans, qui vit à Saint-Omer, dans le Pas-de-Calais, au Nord de la France. Mouloud a rencontré Émilie dans un bar à Saint-Omer, en mai 2023. La jeune Française a écrasé le pied de l’Algérien en dansant. Les deux se sont donné plusieurs rendez-vous par la suite, jusqu’à décider d’emménager ensemble en février 2024. Une histoire en somme toute normale, jusqu’à ce que le couple décide de se marier officiellement. Ils se dirigent à la mairie de Saint-Omer où ils déposent le dossier de mariage en janvier 2026. Mais le 7 avril, le procureur de la République refuse le dossier, soulignant que la demande fait suite à une enquête d’intégration. Concrètement, le problème, c’est que Mouloud est sous OQTF , ce qui ne l’empêche pas légalement de se marier, sauf si l’on soupçonne que son union vise à régulariser sa situation en France, ce que l’avocat du couple nie catégoriquement. « C’est vraiment une histoire d’amour entre les deux », a-t-il déclaré à La Voix Du Nord. Mouloud, qui a quitté l’Algérie en 2012, est pourtant entré en France de manière régulière, en 2022, avec un titre de séjour italien. Il s’installe à Saint-Omer chez son frère, titulaire d’un certificat de résidence de 10 ans, puis demande sa régularisation. La préfecture s’y oppose cependant et le met sous OQTF en 2023. Il tente désespérément de régulariser sa situation Le ressortissant algérien s’exécute et quitte le territoire français. Il prend le bateau vers Alger au départ de Marseille en août 2023, avant de revenir en septembre, avec son permis de séjour italien. Il dépose une deuxième demande de régularisation, mais reçoit une nouvelle OQTF. Assigné à résidence, Mouloud ne baisse pas les bras et demande l’annulation de l’arrêté. Sa requête est cependant refusée par le tribunal administratif de Lille, qui met en avant « une insertion sociale et professionnelle trop maigre » du ressortissant algérien. Ce dernier assure pourtant qu’il prend des cours de français, qu’il fait régulièrement des dons de sang en France et qu’il est doté d’un statut de commerçant ambulant. Sa campagne confie quant à elle au média français qu’elle veut « juste vivre normalement » avec son conjoint algérien. Actuellement, un recours est porté devant la Cour d’appel de Douai. L’avocat du requérant compte miser sur l’article 8 de la Convention européenne des droits de l’homme (CESDH) pour décrocher un titre de séjour à son client, ce qui va lui permettre d’épouser sa dulcinée sans être soupçonné de mariage blanc. L’article Un Algérien rencontre Émilie à Saint-Omer, son OQTF l’empêche de l'épouser est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 2027 Presidency: We couldn’t find another woman to replace Anita — YPP
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Young Progressives Party, YPP, has said it could not find another suitably qualified woman to replace its former presidential candidate, Mrs Anita Zugwai Chukwu, after she withdrew from the 2027 presidential race. The party said Chukwu stepped down after her family raised concerns over the security situation in parts of the country and the extensive travelling and public exposure that would come with the presidential campaign. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Egbeola Wale Martins, on Monday, the party said Dr Peter Agada was subsequently chosen at a Special Presidential Substitution Primary held on Friday, August 21. “Following her withdrawal, the Party explored every available option to fill the Presidential vacancy with another suitably qualified female aspirant. Unfortunately, all efforts in this regard proved abortive,” the YPP said. The party said Chukwu, who emerged from its May 30 presidential primary, formally notified the leadership of her decision in a letter dated August 12, following consultations with members of her immediate and extended family. Rejecting suggestions that she was pressured to quit, the YPP said: “The YPP wishes to state categorically that Mrs. Anita Zugwai Chukwu’s decision was freely and voluntarily taken. There was no coercion, intimidation, pressure or undue influence from the Party or any individual.” The party said it remained proud of Chukwu and appreciated her courage, sacrifice and commitment to its progressive ideals, stressing that Agada’s emergence did not diminish her contribution. It also rejected suggestions that the failure to replace Chukwu with another woman amounted to discrimination, insisting that its commitment to equal opportunity remained firm. “We do not discriminate against anyone on the basis of gender, age, disability or any other status,” the party said. The YPP urged the public and the media to disregard rumours about Chukwu’s withdrawal, saying it remained focused and united ahead of the 2027 general election. items.title: ‘Stabilising voice in times of turbulence’ – Tinubu hails Sultan at 70
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has felicitated with the Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs, Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, on his 70th birthday. President Tinubu said that the Sultan’s 70 years have been a testament to a life lived in service, wisdom, and grace. “For nearly two decades on the throne of your forebears, you have embodied the finest traditions of the Sokoto Caliphate: scholarship, humility, and an unwavering commitment to peace,” he said. In his tribute to the revered spiritual head, the President said: “Today, I join millions of Nigerians in celebrating a remarkable milestone for a remarkable person: His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, the Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs, on his 70th birthday. “Your Eminence, on this day I offer my warmest congratulations to you and your teeming subjects in Sokoto and beyond, on behalf of myself, the First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu, and the government and people of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. “Your seventy years are a testament to a life lived in service, wisdom, and grace. “You have been a stabilising voice in times of turbulence, a bridge-builder across faiths and communities, and a moral compass not only for our Muslim ummah, but for our entire nation. “I have come to know you as a leader who speaks truth with compassion, who counsels patience without weakness, and who champions unity without compromising conviction. “Under your guidance, the Sultanate has continued to promote education, interfaith dialogue, and humanitarian service. Your advocacy for peaceful coexistence, for the girl-child, and for the dignity of every Nigerian reflects the very best of our shared values. “At 70, you remain a towering figure of conscience and counsel. Your palace in Sokoto has become a sanctuary for dialogue, and your words carry weight in every corner of this country. “In moments of grief, you comfort. In moments of division, you unite. In moments of doubt, you remind us of our common humanity and our common destiny as one people under God.” Tinubu said that as President, he deeply values the Sultan’s partnership in nation-building. “Your security support, community development, and the spiritual well-being of our people strengthen the fabric of our republic. Nigeria needs more of the wisdom you so generously offer,” he said. Continuing, the President remarked: “On this landmark birthday, I pray that Allah will continue to grant you many more years in good health, sound mind, and continued strength. May He preserve you for your family, for the Sokoto Caliphate, and for Nigeria. May your reign continue to be a source of blessing, guidance, and honour. “Your Eminence, congratulations once again. May this new decade of your life be your most rewarding yet.” The post ‘Stabilising voice in times of turbulence’ – Tinubu hails Sultan at 70 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana Institution of Surveyors, Roads Ministry agree to strengthen compensation process
items.description: The Ghana Institution of Surveyors (GhIS) and the Ministry of Roads and Highways have agreed to strengthen collaboration on the assessment and payment of compensation to persons affected by road projects. According to a statement issued by the GhIS, the decision was reached at a meeting on Monday, August 24, 2026, between the leadership of the Institution and the Minister for Roads and Highways, Governs Kwame Agbodza. The meeting was attended by the Deputy Minister of Roads and Highways, Alhassan Sayibu Suhuyini; the Chief Director of the Ministry, Ing. Samuel Kwasi Akuaku; and the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Highways Authority, Surv. Mallam Issah Ishak. The GhIS delegation was led by its President, Surv. Emmanuel Kofi Cobbold, and included Past President Surv. Kofi Obeng-Ayirebi, Chief Executive Officer Surv. Sarah Essie Ziddah and other executives of the Institution. The engagement was prompted by recent public concerns raised by the Minister regarding compensation claims linked to some road projects. He had noted discrepancies in valuations between independent assessors and state agencies – a situation he said was contributing to project delays. In an earlier press release, the GhIS said it took the Minister’s concerns seriously, stressing that the Institution does not condone fraud, deliberate inflation of compensation claims, or misrepresentation of valuation evidence. It subsequently requested an audience with the Minister to discuss how to address the underlying reasons that had given rise to such scenarios. During the meeting with the Roads Minister, the GhIS highlighted systemic issues affecting the compensation process, including delays in land acquisition procedures, inadequate stakeholder engagement, inconsistencies in assessment and documentation, and prolonged delays in paying affected property owners. The Institution further observed that statutory procedures governing compulsory acquisition and compensation have not always been applied consistently by all parties. Following the discussions, both sides agreed to continue their engagement through a structured technical process aimed at improving the administration of compensation for road projects. The technical collaboration will involve a review of the compensation process, enhanced exchange of valuation documents and relevant information, stronger stakeholder consultation, and greater adherence to the 1992 Constitution, the Land Act, 2020 (Act 1036), and recognised professional valuation standards. GhIS stressed the need for a transparent, consistent and professionally sound compensation framework to protect the rights of property owners while ensuring value for money for the state. The Institution also reaffirmed its commitment to professional accountability, reminding its members that all compensation claims must be objective, evidence-based and properly documented. Valuations, it added, must be supported by verifiable market data and appropriate professional standards. Members of the Institution are expected to cooperate with any properly constituted review of compensation claims, provided such reviews follow established procedures and due process. GhIS described the meeting as a significant step towards resolving concerns over compensation valuations and establishing a framework for closer collaboration between the surveying profession and the Roads Ministry. The Institution said it remains committed to working with the Ministry and other stakeholders to improve the compensation process, safeguard the constitutional rights of affected persons and uphold professional standards. The statement said further details on the outcomes of the technical engagement will be communicated as discussions progress.

items.title: NBA Confab: Presidential candidates clash on key campaign issues as Gbajabiamila defends FG policies
items.description: By Daniel Abia P/Harcourt More than five presidential candidates of various opposition political parties on Monday clashed as they took on one another on issues bordering on Nigeria’s security architecture and the future of policing,. This is as the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, defended the administration’s push for state police reforms and other policies The second panel session of the day, which featured the presidential candidates, proved to be the most engaging of the conference, with discussions centred on security, police reform, state policing, elections, and fuel subsidy. This contrasted with an earlier session featuring AAC candidate, Omoyele Sowore, senator Dino Melaye, and others, where Melaye’s contributions were largely muted. One of the defining moments of the session was an exchange between Sowore and former Rivers State Governor, Rotimi Amaechi who is also the vice presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress, ADC. Rotimi Amaechi explained that Nigeria economy is very bad, and that one of the ways to stabilize the economy is to create employment and encourage local content ,so that there will be money in people’s pocket for circulation He recalled that he built over 500 primary schools ,over three hundred health centres ,over two hundred roads and crimes drastically reduced , hinting that he fought insecurity to a standstill with adequate intelligence gathering as a sitting governor. Amaechi hinted that he will support community police over state police, because community policing will primarily detect real issues , adding that the Atiku /Amaechi ticket when elected, will be detrabalised in political appointment,to ensure that it will spread across the country, unlike president Tinubu ,who has concentrated all appointments in the agencies around the Yoruba On the question of policing, most candidates on the panel expressed support for the adoption of state police, but the candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Adewale Adebayo pushed instead for a three-tier structure encompassing federal, state, and local government policing. On security, Sowore and Adebayo argued that a change in national leadership was required to address Nigeria’s security challenges, insisting that what they described as “terrorists in the Presidential villa” needed to be voted out for meaningful progress to be made. On the issue of fuel subsidy removal, Sowore said “If there is anybody that has been consistent in the removal of fuel subsidy, it has been me. The question about fuel subsidy is: who are you subsidizing? You are subsidizing the elite. You are subsidizing the governors. The only people who are doing well since the removal of fuel subsidy are the governors of states. “I was a student in 1988. In 1999, they removed subsidy. In 1999, they removed subsidy. We are in 2026, they are still removing subsidy. They are robbing Peter Obi to pay Bola Tinubu. That is what the removal of subsidy is all about. The poor people of this country only benefit from subsidy on petrol, gasoline. There is no subsidy on kerosene. What did they build with it? When it comes to subsidy, transportation policy is important”, he said. The Presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, took a different approach, emphasizing poverty reduction as central to reducing insecurity in the country. “Nigeria must move from a consumption country to a production country. We must invest heavily in agriculture”, Obi said. Despite the differing positions, the panel was described as lively and substantive, with a shared recognition among candidates that major police reforms remain necessary. On democracy and governance, Sowore promised that individuals found to have stolen the nation’s resources would be brought to justice under his administration, if he emerged as the winner of the 2027 presidential election. Also speaking, former Cross River State Governor, Donald Duke, said that getting leadership right remained the fundamental key to addressing Nigeria’s broader challenges. “If we get the leadership right, everything else will fall into place,” he said, decrying the scourge of ethnicity in Nigerian politics and calling for collective efforts to improve the country’s presidential system of government. In a keynote address titled “Policing in Transition,” the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, spoke extensively on the administration’s reforms, why they matter, and the standards by which the administration’s work should be judged. Gbajabiamila said that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had decided to confront a truth the country had ignored for too long by proceeding with the establishment of state police. “Centralized policing without safeguards will bring about more chaos,” he said, explaining that the reform introduces a dual policing system designed to correct existing imbalances. “Nigerians must receive equal protection in every state, regardless of ethnicity, religion, or others,” he added. He stressed the importance of first agreeing on the specific problems the reforms are meant to solve. “It’s important that we agree on the specific nature of the problems we’re trying to solve with these reforms,” he said, citing the problem of police reach as a key example. “Nigeria has one policeman for every 650 people, compared to the international benchmark of one policeman to every 450,” he noted, adding that the disparity becomes even more concerning “when you take note that most policemen are deployed for administrative and escort duties.” Gbajabiamila stressed the need for proper training to prepare officers to enforce the law effectively. “Training must prepare officers to enforce the law properly, professionalism is also very important,” he said, adding that, “policing should become a respected career that every Nigerian chooses.” Addressing the question of oversight, he asked: “Who polices the police?” He argued that “a governor elected by the people cannot be denied the right to carry out executive duties,” but stressed that “a governor shouldn’t be allowed to order the arrest of a political opponent.” He added that “an officer who refuses an unlawful command must be protected as well,” insisting that “these protections mustn’t be just by word of mouth, but by strengthened institutions.” He further addressed concerns around the potential for partisan misuse of police powers under the proposed reforms. items.description: BURKINA-SSR-INFERTILITE-MASCULINE Burkina : Un médecin donne des solutions pour contrer l’infertilité «masculine en progression» Ouagadougou, 24 août 2026 (AIB)-Le président de la Société des Gynécologues et Obstétriciens du Burkina, Pr Charlemagne Ouédraogo, a donné lundi des conseils pour freiner l’infertilité masculine, qui selon lui est en progression. « La qualité du sperme recule, l’infertilité masculine progresse, et pourtant, on en parle peu », a alerté lundi Pr Charlemagne Ouédraogo sur sa page Facebook. Pr Ouédraogo n’a avancé aucune source ou étude pour appuyer son affirmation. Selon une étude menée entre janvier 2019 et décembre 2022, sur les « Aspects épidémiologiques et sémiologiques de l’infertilité masculine au centre hospitalier universitaire Yalgado Ouédraogo du Burkina Faso » a recensé 310 cas d’infertilité masculine. Cependant l’infertilité masculine n’est pas une fatalité, tempère Pr Charlemagne Ouédraogo. Il a exhorté les hommes à «libérer» les testicules au lit ou à la maison car les gonades n'aiment pas la chaleur . Le tabac, l’alcool, la sédentarité, le surpoids, le stress chronique, l’exposition à la chaleur et autre perturbateurs endocriniens sont des facteurs à risque, prévient le médecin. Le spécialiste a également recommandé une alimentation riche en fruits, en légumes, en oméga-3 et en antioxydants, une activité physique régulière et un sommeil de qualité. Agence d’information du Burkina JT/rbk/ata
